observations: A manual treadle sewing machine mounted in a wooden cabinet/table with a cast-iron treadle base, shown in 4 angles.
The machine head has a decal reading something like 'MERCURY' visible in photos 1 and 2.
Visible paint chipping, rust-like orange/red patches, and scuffed chrome on the machine body in photos 1-3.
No electric motor, power cord, or plug is visible anywhere; the machine is treadle (foot-pedal) operated.
No manual, accessories, or extra parts are shown in any photo.
Background shows an outdoor roadside setting with a phone-charging signboard, consistent with a shop display, not a home.

claims.evidence: Photos 1-3 show paint chipping, rust-colored spots, and worn chrome on the machine body.
Only a 'Mercury' decal is visible; no country-of-origin marking or plate is readable in any photo.
No electric motor, cord, or plug is visible in any photo; the machine appears to be a manual treadle type, so a running 'motor' claim does not match what is shown.

claims.claim: All accessories and the original manual
claims.evidence: No manual, bobbins, extra needles, or accessory case are shown in any of the 4 photos.

claims.claim: Never serviced because nothing ever went wrong
claims.evidence: Service history cannot be confirmed from photos; visible wear and rust suggest age and use that would typically need maintenance.

risks.risk: Stitching mechanism may be seized, misaligned, or skip stitches despite visual appearance of completeness.
risks.proof: A short video clip of the treadle being pedaled and the needle/feed dog moving while stitching a scrap of fabric.

risks.risk: Extent of rust/corrosion on internal gears and shuttle hook, not just surface paint, could affect function.
risks.proof: Close-up photos of the shuttle/bobbin area and underside gears.
risks.if_unproven: priced as heavily worn/cosmetically and mechanically degraded

risks.risk: Claimed 'motor' may not exist (purely treadle-operated), so any buyer expecting electric operation would be misled.
risks.proof: A clear photo or statement confirming whether this is treadle-only or has a hidden/detachable electric motor.
risks.if_unproven: priced as treadle-only, no electric motor

risks.risk: Missing accessories (bobbins, extra needles, manual) would lower value versus a 'complete set' claim.
risks.proof: A photo laying out all included accessories and the manual together.

risks.risk: Cabinet/table structural integrity (wood joints, treadle linkage) not fully visible for wear or cracks.
risks.proof: Photos of the underside of the table and the treadle linkage joints.
risks.if_unproven: priced as cabinet in unknown/worn structural condition

proof_requests: Video of the machine being treadled and actually stitching fabric.
Close-up of the brand/model plate and any serial number or 'Made in' marking.
Photo of all accessories and the manual laid out together.
Close-up of the shuttle/bobbin case and underside mechanism.
Photo of the full underside of the cabinet and treadle linkage.
response.reason: The item is clearly identifiable as a worn Mercury-branded treadle sewing machine in a cabinet, so it can be priced at worst case (cosmetic wear, unproven working condition, no confirmed accessories) even though several seller claims are unverified or contradicted.
